newsitem.title: USA: Republican leader faults Clinton on Medicare.
newsitem.headline: Republican leader faults Clinton on Medicare.

text.p: Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott accused President Bill Clinton on Sunday of being irresponsible in dealing with Medicare.
"On Medicare, he's been irresponsible, he's misled the people, he's misinformed them," Lott said of Clinton's campaign claims on Medicare. "It's been disingenuous."
"He's going to have to basically admit the problem is there, it's more serious than he has acknowledged, and then we'll work together," Lott said on NBC's "Meet the Press" program.
Clinton accused Republican rival Bob Dole of wanting to slash Medicare, threatening the health care of 38 million elderly and disabled people in the program.

Both Democrats and Republicans agree that at least some reforms must be made to the program to help balance the federal budget and ensure that Medicare can handle the baby boomers who start retiring around 2010.
But they disagree on how much to restrain spending, or how to revamp the popular program.
Republicans kept control of the House and Senate in Tuesday's elections while Clinton won a second term.
Lott said that the Republicans would look at any Medicare plan that Clinton proposes, but he was not in favor of naming a bipartisan commission to find a solution.
"I don't like the idea of kicking the ball every time, punting the ball, saying, oh, let a commission do it," Lott said. "We have a responsibility. We can do it ourselves."
